newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks foreseen opening lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks foreseen opening lower.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were seen opening lower on Tuesday, with the markets taking some profits after Monday's record close at 6567.
Analysts said markets were likely to be watching economic indicators due today, especially factory orders at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, for signs of quicker economic growth.
"We're probably going to get a lower opening," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood. "The market is probably nervous about the pace of the economy picking up."
Such basic industrial stocks as paper, chemical and oil in particular could see profit-taking after rises during Monday's record run.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said one worrisome point was continued weakness in bonds, which reflects concern about the pace of economic growth. Before the markets opened on Tuesday, the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 2/16 to yield 6.77.
The factory orders number will affect bonds more than equities, and bonds are "the key to the stock market," he said.
A consensus by economists is for a 0.6 percent drop in November factory orders, against a gain of 0.9 percent in October.
Other data due today include the BTM/Schroders retail chain store report for the week ended January 4.
Also, the Redbook retail index will be released at 1455 EST/1955 GMT for the week ended January 4.
London stocks were down, with the FTSE 100 index off 14.8 to 4092. U.S. shares in London were mostly flat in relatively quiet trade, with blue chips leading the way.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 average plunged 549.81 points to close at 18,896.19 as the market was beset by lingering worries about the economy.
The dollar was at 115.24 yen in late Tokyo trade. In Europe the dollar was steady, holding above 1.56 marks and 115.20 yen. The Standard and Poors 500 futures index was off 0.80 to 749.90.
